name: Secondary Non-Traumatic Avascular Necrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Presence of localized joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing
MRI or radiographic evidence of bone marrow edema, subchondral lucency, or crescent sign
History of corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or systemic diseases associated with ischemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is rarely required; diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
No specific laboratory test diagnostic for avascular necrosis
imaging: MRI showing bone marrow edema and early ischemic changes
X-ray demonstrating subchondral radiolucency (crescent sign), sclerosis, and eventual bone collapse
CT scan may show detailed bony architecture changes
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible association with thrombophilia or coagulation disorders in some cases
other: History of corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or systemic diseases such as lupus or sickle cell disease

distinguishingFeatures: History of acute trauma preceding symptoms
Radiological evidence of fracture or dislocation
Elevated inflammatory markers and positive joint fluid cultures
Gradual onset with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation on imaging
Less severe early pain compared to avascular necrosis

redFlags: Sudden worsening of joint pain indicating possible bone collapse
references: Moya-Angeler J, et al. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head: pathophysiology and current concepts of treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2015;97(19):1620-1629.
Assouline-Dayan Y, et al. Pathogenesis and natural history of osteonecrosis. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2002;32(2):94-124.
